test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 07 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following best describes the main purpose of developing Genetically Modified Organisms (GMOs) in agriculture ?

options.text: To reduce the cost of manual weeding and irrigation only
To improve crop yield, pest resistance, and nutritional quality
To eliminate the need for fertilizers and pesticides entirely
To grow crops only in artificial laboratory environments

solution:
The correct answer is __**To improve crop yield, pest resistance, and nutritional quality**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Genetically Modified Organisms (GMOs)** are developed with the aim of addressing challenges such as low crop yields, pest infestations, and poor nutritional quality.
 
• GMOs are engineered to have **higher resistance to pests and diseases**, reducing the need for chemical pesticides.
 
• They are modified to enhance **nutritional profiles**, such as adding vitamins or nutrients to crops like rice and maize.
 
• Improving crop yield through genetic modification ensures better food security for growing populations worldwide.
 
• GMOs contribute to sustainable farming practices by minimizing resource use and addressing environmental concerns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Genetic Engineering:**

 
 
• Genetic engineering involves modifying the DNA of organisms to introduce desirable traits.
 
• It uses techniques such as CRISPR, gene splicing, and recombinant DNA technology.
 
 
 
• **Golden Rice:**
 
 
• A genetically modified variety of rice enriched with vitamin A to combat deficiencies in developing countries.
 
• It is an example of using GMOs to improve nutritional quality.
 
 
 
• **Pest Resistance:**
 
 
• Crops like Bt cotton and Bt corn are engineered with Bacillus thuringiensis genes to combat pests naturally.
 
• This reduces dependence on chemical pesticides, benefiting both farmers and the environment.
 
 
 
• **Controversies Surrounding GMOs:**
 
 
• GMOs face criticism over potential health impacts, environmental risks, and ethical concerns.
 
• Regulatory measures and scientific assessments are in place to ensure safety.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Agriculture:**
 
 
• GMOs play a significant role in addressing challenges like climate change, soil degradation, and water scarcity.
 
• They are part of modern sustainable farming practices aimed at feeding growing populations efficiently.
